description: Server-level health for the redis StatefulSet in namespace data (app.kubernetes.io/instance=redis), the shared cache every app reaches at redis.data:6379 on its own logical database. Hardcoded to this one server. There is no redis_exporter yet (components/monitoring is a placeholder), so memory, CPU and network come from cAdvisor and kube-state-metrics - there are no keyspace, hit-rate, client or eviction metrics. Workload, Logs, Dependencies, Resources and GitHub are tabs, and a tab only queries while it is open. GitHub reads kubed-io/redis through the github datasource. The masthead at the top is pinned and shared: the App masthead library panel, driven by the app_namespace and app_name constants, showing identity (workload, namespace, image tag) and the current verdict as pills. It reads kube-state-metrics with instant queries, so it always shows NOW and ignores the time range. Overview is a collapsible row of the numbers that do follow the range - collapse it to put the tabs under the masthead and focus. The masthead's 'up' pill replaces the old Up since tile: save "" and appendonly no mean nothing survives a restart, so it is also how old every consumer's cache is.

panels.description:
Working set as a share of maxmemory (3gb, set by REDIS_MAXMEMORY in components/resources).

**Interesting when:** past 100%. allkeys-lru starts evicting keys from every database — and because this is a shared cache, the app that loses keys is not necessarily the one that filled it.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description:
Share of CPU periods over the range in which the 1-CPU limit stopped the container mid-work.

**Interesting when:** anything sustained. Redis is single-threaded, so throttling reaches clients as latency on every command.
panels.title: Throttled

panels.description:
Kubernetes Warning events for this app over the range, read from the kube-events stream in Loki rather than the API — the API drops events after about an hour, Loki keeps them.

**Careful:** Loki has no event type label, so Warning is matched by a regex on the reason. A Normal event whose reason contains one of those words is counted too.
panels.title: Warnings

panels.description:
Memory in use, against the two ceilings that matter.

**Interesting when:** it approaches the orange dashed line — maxmemory (3gb), where allkeys-lru starts evicting keys from every database. The red dashed line above is the 4Gi container limit, where the kernel OOMKills instead.

**Careful:** rss above working set is fragmentation Redis has not handed back, not extra data.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description:
Pod network throughput.

**Interesting when:** you want a command rate. There is no redis exporter feeding this dashboard, so this is the closest proxy — every GET and SET is a round trip, so load from the consumers shows up here first.
panels.title: Network

panels.description: Why a container last died. OOMKilled here means the container hit its memory limit.
panels.title: Last terminated reason

panels.description: Percent of CPU periods throttled by the limit. Sustained non-zero means commands are queuing.
panels.title: CPU throttling

panels.description:
Redis logs at notice level, which is almost entirely lifecycle — a burst of seven notice lines is one start.

**Interesting when:** warning (#) appears. That is the real signal. A spike in *other* alongside a start is worth reading too: those are lines outside Redis's own format — the SIGTERM handler and kubelet messages — so the pair means a restart.

targets.expr: sum by (level) (count_over_time({namespace="data", app="redis"} | regexp `^\d+:[XCSM] \d{1,2} \w{3} \d{4} [\d:.]+ (?P<sym>[.*#-]) ` | label_format level=`{{ if eq .sym "#" }}warning{{ else if eq .sym "*" }}notice{{ else if eq .sym "-" }}verbose{{ else if eq .sym "." }}debug{{ else }}other{{ end }}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Log volume by level

panels.description:
Every line, unfiltered. Redis is quiet enough to stream raw — starts, shutdowns and warnings only.

The symbol after the timestamp is the level: `*` notice, `#` warning.

Which apps use this Redis, and which logical database index each one owns.

**Careful:** hand-maintained from the index registry in the redis README. Every consumer reaches Redis through a connection string in its own config and nothing in the cluster declares the dependency — which is why every edge is dashed.
